title: Two aspects: the process and the result

blocks.text: In Russian almost every action is expressed by a pair of verbs. Such twin-verbs differ only in what we call aspect, and otherwise have the same basic meaning.
The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself. The perfective aspect places the emphasis on the result of the action.

The verb **писать** is called imperfective and has the following two meanings: 1. to be writing, to be in the process of writing for a certain period of time (in the present, past or future): *Я сейчас пишу. Вчера я весь вечер писал. Завтра я всё утро буду писать.* 2. to write habitually (often, always, etc.): *Я каждый день пишу.*

The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).

head: The general idea of an imperfective verb is:
of a perfective verb is:
rows: 1. to do (to be doing) something for a period of time: *Я долго писал письмо.*
1. to complete the action and thus to achieve a result: *Я написал письмо; вот оно на столе.*
2. to do something habitually: *Я всегда пишу письма по-русски.*
2. to do something once: *Ему я написал по-английски.*

blocks.text: Both the imperfective and perfective forms of a Russian verb are to be memorized as a pair because there are no definite rules of forming one aspect from the other one: some twin-verbs differ only by a prefix in the perfective aspect; some have other changes: **читать** — **прочитать**, **получать** — **получить**. Sometimes, even two quite different verbs make an imperfective-perfective pair: **говорить** — **сказать**.
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.
Further sentences, so that every pattern above is practised: from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English.

exercises.prompt: When and where was Beethoven born?
exercises.why: **родиться → родился** — past tense, masc.: drop -ться, add -лся.

exercises.prompt: Looks like the transmission belt broke.
exercises.why: **сломаться → сломался** — past tense, masc.: drop -ться, add -лся.

exercises.prompt: Did you think Marseilles was the capital city of France?
exercises.why: **думать → думал** — past tense, masc.: drop -ть, add -л.

exercises.q: Ни у кого не ___ (возникать) никаких вопросов касательно плана.
exercises.prompt: No one had any questions about the plan.
exercises.why: **возникать → возникало** — past tense, neut.: drop -ть, add -ло.

exercises.q: Я думаю, она ___ (осознавать), что на неё заглядываются многие парни.
exercises.prompt: I think she was conscious of being stared at by many boys.
exercises.why: **осознавать → осознавала** — past tense, fem.: drop -ть, add -ла.

exercises.prompt: Tom waited a moment before replying.
exercises.why: **выждать → выждал** — past tense, masc.: drop -ть, add -л.

exercises.q: Несомненное достоинство автоматических дверей в том, что люди больше не ___ (разносить) заразу через дверные ручки.
exercises.prompt: A definite advantage of automatic doors is that people can't spread their contagious diseases by touching door handles.
exercises.why: **разносить → разносят** — present-type form, 3rd person plural: ending -ят belongs to the second (и) conjugation.

exercises.prompt: The world is not going to be saved by legislation.
exercises.why: **спасти → спасёт** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Computers will save you a lot of time.
exercises.why: **сберечь → сберегут** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Том ___ (быть) иметь право на условно-досрочное освобождение в следующем году.
exercises.prompt: Tom will be eligible for parole next year.
exercises.why: **быть → будет** — future of быть: 3rd person singular.

exercises.prompt: You're not going to get anything out of this slacker.
exercises.why: **быть → будет** — future of быть: 3rd person singular.

exercises.prompt: Bogdan said he would be there tomorrow.
exercises.why: **быть → будет** — future of быть: 3rd person singular.
